name: Strategic petroleum reserves (salt caverns, rock caverns)
aliases: Strategic petroleum reserves (salt caverns, rock caverns)
principle: Governments hold crude in leached salt caverns or lined rock caverns for supply emergencies. The US reserve has an authorised capacity of 714 million barrels at four Gulf Coast sites (Bryan Mound, Big Hill, West Hackberry, Bayou Choctaw).

process_steps.name: Leach cavern with water and fill with crude

source.note: US DOE, Strategic Petroleum Reserve page, read 25 October 2026

advantages: Fast release capacity via marine terminals (2.22 MMbbl/d contracted plus 0.4 MMbbl/d DOE-owned)
limitations: Rock caverns and non-US reserves are not covered by the source read
